h1:
Phitsanulok Food
Worth Trying at Least Once
intro: Phitsanulok is the kind of city most people only pass through to pay respects to the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat Buddha, but the food here is more fun than you'd expect. There are riverside noodle shops on the Nan River where you sit with your feet dangling over the water, flying morning glory that gets stir-fried in a burst of flame then tossed across the air to a waiter holding a plate, plus chewy Bang Krathum sun-dried bananas, mi sua noodles, and a steady stream of new cafes popping up around town. We've pulled together the good stuff that travelers actually stop to eat and take home, all in one place.

blocks.html: Most of what makes Phitsanulok's food distinctive is tied to the Nan River running through the middle of town — the noodle shops that set their tables right at the water's edge so you can sit with your feet dangling, and the rice-soup spots famous for the flaming flying-morning-glory show. Head a little out of town and you run into souvenirs like Bang Krathum sun-dried banana and mi sua noodles. We've sorted the food into groups so it's easy to follow along, from the signature dishes you have to try, to the riverside spots, the province's classic souvenirs, and chill cafes around the city.

blocks.text: Signature dishes you have to try

blocks.html: Let's start with the dishes that instantly come to mind when you say Phitsanulok. These four are the ones travelers come specifically to try, and the flavors that keep people coming back for a second visit.

items.name: Riverside dangling-leg noodles on the Nan
items.blurb: Phitsanulok's signature is the noodle shops that line up long tables right along the Nan River so you can sit with your feet dangling over the water and watch the view while you eat. There are several noodle types to pick from, both tom yum and clear broth, with a mellow, slightly sweet soup. It's an atmosphere you'd be hard pressed to find anywhere else. The well-known spots sit along the river near Ekathotsarot Bridge.

items.name: Flying morning glory (Wirote Phochana)
items.blurb: An old rice-soup institution that's the original home of flying morning glory. Order the high-flame morning glory and the cook stir-fries it in a roaring blaze out front, then tosses the greens sailing through the air to someone holding a plate on the other side. The show has become the image people associate with the city. The dish itself is boldly seasoned and pairs perfectly with hot rice soup.

items.name: Bang Krathum sun-dried banana
items.blurb: The province's number-one souvenir, made from Mali Ong cultivar bananas sun-dried until chewy and soft, naturally sweet with no added sugar. Bang Krathum district is famous enough for it to earn GI registration. Some makers do rolled sun-dried banana, honey-baked banana, or chocolate-dipped versions. A souvenir people are always happy to receive.
items.meta: Souvenir · Bang Krathum district + shops in town

items.name: Phitsanulok mi sua noodles
items.blurb: Chewy mi sua noodles made the traditional way, popularly stir-fried with soy sauce or with egg. It works both as a one-plate dish in the shops and as a dried-noodle souvenir to carry home and cook yourself. You can find it at the souvenir shops around Wat Yai and the markets in town.

items.name: Sai miang & snacks around Wat Yai
items.blurb: The area around Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) is lined with local snacks and souvenirs — sai miang, sun-dried banana, mi sua, and Thai sweets all in a row. Easy to swing by after paying respects to the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat Buddha, and the spot where most people stop to grab souvenirs.

items.name: Fish rice soup & made-to-order food on the Nan
items.blurb: In the evenings along the Nan River, rice-soup and made-to-order shops stay open late, perfect for an easygoing, wallet-friendly way to close out the day. Order fish rice soup, stir-fried vegetables and a few standout dishes to share. The cool breeze off the river hits just right.

blocks.title: Tips for the dangling-leg noodles
blocks.html: Most of the dangling-leg shops sell from morning to afternoon. If you want a good riverside table, going before noon is more comfortable. During the rainy-season high water some shops may rearrange their seating, so consider calling ahead to check if you're coming specifically for this atmosphere.

blocks.html: The charm of eating in Phitsanulok is the Nan River running through the middle of town. Both banks have noodle shops, rice-soup spots, and a night bazaar that opens in the evening. We've picked the shops and spots that reviewers mention most often and that are still actually open.

items.name: Riverside dangling-leg noodles on the Nan
items.blurb: The spot where people come to snap a photo sitting with their feet dangling, eating noodles by the water. Relaxed atmosphere and a cool breeze, best in the late morning to afternoon. Order tom yum or clear-broth noodles with meatballs and settle in to watch the boats and river view.

items.name: Riverside night bazaar
items.blurb: An evening market along the river with a long stretch of snacks and food shops — fried food, grilled skewers, sweets, and sit-down riverside spots. A pleasant place to graze in the evening, and the city's go-to for an easygoing, budget-friendly dinner.
items.meta: Phutthabucha Rd, riverside · Opens in the evening

items.name: Rice-soup & made-to-order shops near Wat Yai
items.blurb: Across from Wat Yai along the river there are several rice-soup and made-to-order shops to choose from, great for ending the day after visiting the temple. Order a few standout dishes to share with hot rice soup and catch the cool breeze off the water.

blocks.title: Best time to eat along the Nan
blocks.html: Morning to late morning suits the dangling-leg noodles and the soft early light, while the evening belongs to the night bazaar and rice-soup shops. Come on a weekday and it's more relaxed to walk around than on a busy weekend.

Over the past few years, plenty of cafes have sprung up in Phitsanulok — both serious-coffee spots and photo-corner places. Many are in town and around Naresuan University. We've picked a few to try depending on your mood, from places to settle in and work for a while to quick photo stops.

items.name: Seattle Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: A serious-coffee cafe with well-chosen beans and a warm street-style vibe, great for coffee lovers after a sharp espresso or drip.

items.name: Hammock Cafe
items.blurb: A laid-back spot to relax with cute photo corners, good for a midday stop or a long, easy hang in the afternoon.

items.name: The Letter Coffee Bar
items.blurb: A city cafe people talk about for its drinks and desserts, easy to slot into a day of walking around town from late morning to afternoon.

items.name: Groom Cat Craft Cafe
items.blurb: A cat cafe with kitties waiting to greet you upstairs and a drinks-and-snacks zone downstairs, perfect for cat lovers who want to hang out with the little ones.

blocks.title: Cafe hopping in town
blocks.html: The cafes in central Phitsanulok aren't far apart — a few minutes by car or motorbike taxi and you're there. You can easily plan to hit 2–3 in an afternoon. Many close early in the evening, so it's worth checking their hours on the shop's page first.

blocks.text: What to bring home as a souvenir

blocks.html: Phitsanulok is an easy souvenir town to shop, because most of what's on offer is dried goods that keep for a long time. The area around Wat Yai and the markets in town have shops lined up side by side, so you can grab everything in one go.

items.name: Bang Krathum sun-dried banana
items.blurb: The number-one souvenir — chewy, soft and naturally sweet, available rolled, honey-baked, or chocolate-dipped. Pick the individually wrapped kind and it's easy to hand out.

items.name: Mi sua (dried noodles)
items.blurb: Handmade chewy mi sua noodles you can carry home to stir-fry yourself — a local souvenir people associate with Phitsanulok.

items.name: Sai miang & dried goods around Wat Yai
items.blurb: Sai miang, sun-dried banana, Thai sweets and assorted dried goods are all gathered around Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat — easy to grab in one stop after visiting the temple.

faq.q: What food should you try in Phitsanulok?
faq.a: Riverside dangling-leg noodles on the Nan are the number-one dish people think of. Next is flying morning glory, stir-fried over high flame and tossed through the air as a show at Wirote Phochana. For souvenirs, go for Bang Krathum sun-dried banana and dried mi sua noodles to carry home.

faq.q: What are dangling-leg noodles, and where do you eat them?
faq.a: They're noodle shops that set tables along the Nan River so you can sit with your feet dangling over the water while you eat and watch the view. The famous spots are along the river in town near Ekathotsarot Bridge, around ฿40–70 a bowl, open morning to afternoon. We'd suggest going before noon to grab a good riverside table.

faq.q: Where's the original shop for Phitsanulok flying morning glory?
faq.a: The original is Wirote Phochana, an old rice-soup institution in town. Branch 1 is along Mittraphap Road. The highlight is ordering the high-flame morning glory — the cook stir-fries it in a blaze out front and tosses the greens sailing across to someone holding a plate on the other side.

faq.q: Where's the best place to buy Phitsanulok sun-dried banana?
faq.a: The original source is Bang Krathum district, which holds GI registration. But if you're not heading out of town, you can buy it at the souvenir shops around Wat Yai and the markets in town. Pick the individually wrapped kind — it's easy to hand out and keeps for a long time.

faq.q: Are there good cafes to sit in Phitsanulok?
faq.a: There are several in town and around Naresuan University, from serious-coffee spots like Seattle Specialty Coffee to chill photo spots like Hammock Cafe and The Letter Coffee Bar. Most cafes aren't far apart, so you can easily plan to hit 2–3 in an afternoon.
